component.name: crypto
component.title: Crypto (JCE)
component.description: Sign message bodies and verify their signatures with java.security.Signature of the Java Cryptography Architecture.
component.label: security,transformation

algorithm.description: The standard name of the signature algorithm of the Java Cryptography Architecture, for example SHA256withRSA or SHA256withECDSA. It must match the type of the key, and the sign and verify endpoints must use the same algorithm.

alias.description: The alias of the keystore entry: the sign operation signs with its private key, and the verify operation verifies with its certificate. If not set and the keystore holds exactly one entry, that entry is used.

certificateName.description: The name of a java.security.cert.Certificate bean in the registry to use as the certificate option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

keystore.description: The keystore that holds the private key for the sign operation and the certificate for the verify operation. The alias option selects the entry, or the only entry is used when the keystore holds exactly one. An entry found in the keystore is used instead of the privateKey, certificate and publicKey options.

keystoreName.description: The name of a java.security.KeyStore bean in the registry to use as the keystore option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

privateKey.description: The private key that the sign operation signs with. A private key found in the keystore under the alias is used instead. The verify operation does not use it.

privateKeyName.description: The name of a java.security.PrivateKey bean in the registry to use as the privateKey option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

provider.description: The name of the security provider that provides the signature algorithm, for example BC for Bouncy Castle. The provider must be installed. If not set, the first installed provider that supports the algorithm is used.

publicKeyName.description: The name of a java.security.PublicKey bean in the registry to use as the publicKey option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

secureRandomName.description: The name of a java.security.SecureRandom bean in the registry to use as the secureRandom option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

signatureHeaderName.description: The name of the header in which the sign operation stores the Base64 encoded signature, and from which the verify operation reads it. If not set, CamelDigitalSignature is used.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

bufferSize.label: advanced
bufferSize.description: The size in bytes of the buffer that reads the message body into the signature. It must be at least 1.

certificate.label: advanced
certificate.description: The certificate whose public key the verify operation checks the signature with. A certificate found in the keystore under the alias is used instead, and this option is used instead of the publicKey option.

clearHeaders.label: advanced
clearHeaders.description: Whether to remove the headers whose names start with CamelSignature or CamelDigitalSignature after the operation succeeds. The sign operation removes them before it sets the signature header, and the verify operation also removes the signature header when its name matches.

configuration.label: advanced
configuration.description: The configuration with the default options of all endpoints. Each endpoint gets a copy of it, and the options of the endpoint change only that copy.

keyStoreParameters.label: advanced
keyStoreParameters.description: The KeyStoreParameters (resource, type, password and provider of the keystore) that create the keystore of the keystore option. The keystore is loaded when this option is set.

publicKey.label: advanced
publicKey.description: The public key that the verify operation checks the signature with, when neither the keystore nor the certificate option gives a certificate. The sign operation does not use it.

secureRandom.label: advanced
secureRandom.description: The java.security.SecureRandom that the sign operation passes to Signature.initSign. If not set, the signature provider uses its own source of randomness.

password.label: security
password.description: The password of the private key entry in the keystore, which the sign operation needs to read the key. It is not the password of the keystore itself.

CamelSignaturePrivateKey.description: The PrivateKey that should be used to sign the message

CamelSignaturePublicKeyOrCert.description: The Certificate or PublicKey that should be used to verify the signature. When set, it is used instead of the publicKey, certificate or keystore of the endpoint

CamelDigitalSignature.description: The signature of the message, set by the sign operation and read by the verify operation (the signatureHeaderName option changes the header name)

CamelSignatureKeyStoreAlias.description: The alias used to query the KeyStore for keys and Certificates to be used in signing and verifying exchanges

CamelSignatureKeyStorePassword.description: The password used to access an aliased PrivateKey in the KeyStore.

producerIn.description: The payload to sign or verify, read as a stream: text, bytes, a stream or a file. A Map, a POJO or a number fails: marshal it first. A stream body is cached, so the next step still gets it. No body: sign signs an empty payload, and verify fails with a SignatureException. The signature is not in the body: sign sets it, Base64 encoded, in the CamelDigitalSignature header (signatureHeaderName), which verify reads

producerOut.description: The body is unchanged: a signature that does not verify fails the exchange with a SignatureException

cryptoOperation.description: The operation: sign creates a signature of the message body, and verify checks the signature of the message body. It is the part of the URI after crypto:, as in crypto:sign:name.

name.description: A name of your choice that tells the endpoints apart, as in crypto:sign:name. The component does not use it.
